newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gold ends up on overseas buying.
newsitem.headline: HK gold ends up on overseas buying.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended up on Friday from New York's previous close on buying interest from Japanese traders, despite losing some of those gains in afternoon sales, bullion dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$352.30/80 an ounce Friday against New York's US$351.90/352.40 close on Thursday.
The morning session saw buying activity from Japanese traders, as well as some short-covering.
But dealers said that activity had been so slow it was hard to pinpoint any firm trend.
"Below $351 per ounce there is interest to buy and at $353 people want to sell," said one gold trader at an international bank.
Traders said the possibility of Swiss gold sales to fund a foundation for Holocaust victims was overshadowing the market.
Local gold ended HK$10 higher at HK$3,267 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose from +3.50 to +8.00.
